rounds.text: Allcargo Terminals Ltd trades at an attractive P/E of 15.7x and a price-to-book of 1.92x [E1, E2], which compare favorably against broader sector benchmarks such as a sector P/E of -411.65x and a sector P/B of 23.98x [E6, E7]. The company demonstrates robust fundamental efficiency, highlighted by a strong trailing return on equity of 12.9% alongside a 3-year median ROE of 18% [E13, E19], outperforming the sector benchmark ROE of 6.81% [E9]. Furthermore, cash generation is exceptionally strong, delivering ₹ 125 Cr in operating cash flow and ₹ 113 Cr in free cash flow for March 2026, with an elite cash conversion ratio of 3.12x meaning profits are fully and cleanly backed by cash [E25, E26, E27]. Momentum in the underlying business is clearly accelerating, evidenced by recent quarterly performance showing year-on-year sales growth of 17% and net profit growth of 36% [E55, E57, E64]. These stellar fundamental tailwinds are amplified by a supportive macro services sector backdrop featuring a tailwind score of up to +0.64 [E63, E65] and an EV/EBITDA of just 7.68x compared to a sector benchmark of 28.21x [E11]. Conceded: debt-to-equity stands at an elevated 1.49x with borrowings reaching ₹ 529 Cr [E29, E30].

Allcargo Terminals Ltd carries significant structural and valuation risks that are unsupported by its current market price. The business is heavily leveraged with a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.49x as borrowings swelled to Rs 529 Cr in March 2026, accompanied by flagging concerns over a low interest coverage ratio [E29, E30, E51]. This heavy debt burden is compounded by massive contingent liabilities of Rs 196 Cr and a zero dividend yield that leaves shareholders empty-handed despite reported profits [E4, E53]. Valuation metrics confirm the stock is fundamentally overvalued, with a discounted cash flow model showing an intrinsic value of Rs 17 against a market price of ₹ 23.4, resulting in a negative margin of safety of -41.2% [E2, E36, E37]. Operational momentum is also deteriorating, demonstrated by a 3-year compounded profit growth of -14%, a trailing twelve-month profit contraction of -24%, and declining operating margins [E16, E17, E21]. Furthermore, institutional exodus is clear as foreign institutional holding dropped to 5.34% and domestic institutional holding fell to 0.21% since September 2023 [E33, E34]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong short-term top-line and bottom-line growth alongside solid free cash flow generation of Rs 113 Cr in March 2026 [E27, E55, E57].

Nevertheless, this short-term bounce masks a severe multi-year contraction, with 3-year compounded profit growth at -14% and trailing twelve-month profit growth at -24% [E16, E17]. Yet these multiples sit atop a risky balance sheet where debt-to-equity is 1.49x with borrowings rising to Rs 529 Cr, a low interest coverage ratio, and Rs 196 Cr in contingent liabilities [E29, E30, E51, E53]. Conceded: ROE is 12.54% [E9]. Even so, institutional trust has drained away as foreign and domestic institutional holdings dropped significantly between September 2023 and June 2026 [E33, E34], leaving the stock lagging with an RS rating of 21 and trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E41, E42, E60].
